extracted.intended_audience: agency counsel, federal judges, administrative law practitioners, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the Administrative Procedure Act's requirements for publication, definitions, reviewability of agency action, stays pending review, and the scope/standards of judicial review of agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory venue designations
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes providing for judicial review often designate the venue by relation to the matters involved (e.g., 'any circuit court of appeals ... wherein the unfair labor practice ... was alleged' or where the person aggrieved resides or transacts business).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such special venue provisions (and general venue statutes like 28 U.S.C. 112) continue in effect for suits against Government agencies; see cited precedents (Kentucky Natural Gas Corp. v. Public Service Comm.; Scientific Mfg. Co. v. Walker).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior, adequate, and exclusive review (section 10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where statutes expressly or as interpreted require parties to resort to some special statutory form of judicial review which is prior in time and adequate to the case, that prior, adequate, and exclusive review operates to preclude challenge in enforcement proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision restates existing law; Congress intended section 10 to be integrated with existing statutory judicial review schemes. Courts may conclude legislative intent to make review exclusive from statutory context (example: United States v. Ruzicka).

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of primary jurisdiction and exhaustion preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10(b) leaves intact the doctrine of primary jurisdiction and the requirements of exhaustion of administrative remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may require matters (e.g., reasonableness of filed tariffs) be first presented to the appropriate agency; adequacy of exclusive review and whether opportunity for prior judicial review was waived must be determined case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of defense in enforcement proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In many situations the alleged invalidity of agency action may be set up as a defense to a civil or criminal enforcement proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: But where Congress has provided an exclusive statutory route requiring prior administrative proceedings and record-building, collateral defense may be precluded; balance the statutory scheme and legislative intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewability: final agency action or statutorily reviewable action (section 10(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every agency action made reviewable by statute and every final agency action for which there is no other adequate remedy in any court shall be subject to judicial review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation must account for other statutory and case law; does not make reviewable action precluded by statute or committed to agency discretion, nor does it override special and adequate review procedures Congress provided (e.g., Customs Court).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency action is not reviewable when (1) statutes preclude judicial review, or (2) agency action is by law committed to agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, where Congress provided special and adequate review procedures, section 10(c) does not furnish additional judicial remedies; existing exclusive jurisdictions remain intact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'agency action' (section 2(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Agency action' includes the whole or part of every agency rule, order, license, sanction, relief, or the equivalent or denial thereof, or failure to act."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This broad definition brings rules within section 10's coverage, but other provisions (and legislative history) limit abstract review of rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality requirement for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Only 'final' agency action is reviewable under the subsection unless otherwise made reviewable by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaning of 'final' is informed by prior constructions in regulatory statutes; an action which is finally operative and decisive is reviewable, whereas action automatically stayable on further proceedings is not final.

rubrics_metrics.name: No abstract review of all rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10(c) was not intended to provide for judicial review in the abstract of all rules (i.e., a general, abstract declaratory review of rules of general applicability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of rules is appropriate when applied to a particular person or under accepted declaratory judgment principles where there is an interest and present injury; declaratory judgment doctrine may need adaptation for agency fact-determination issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-reviewability of preliminary, procedural, or intermediate actions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Any preliminary, procedural, or intermediate agency action or ruling not directly reviewable shall be subject to review upon the review of the final agency action."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders setting matters for hearing and other intermediate orders are generally not directly or collaterally reviewable (citing cases like FPC v. Metropolitan Edison; Myers v. Bethlehem). Such questions are reviewed as part of final agency action review (see section 10(e) and section 10(c)'s second sentence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reconsideration and statutory prerequisites to review
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency action otherwise final is final for purposes of the subsection whether or not any application for reconsideration, reopening, rehearing, or appeal to superior agency authority has been presented or determined—unless a statute expressly requires such an application as a prerequisite to judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutes like the Federal Power Act and Natural Gas Act that expressly require reconsideration remain conditions precedent to judicial review; common statutory provisions may bar courts from considering objections not raised before the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency rules requiring internal appeal as prerequisite to judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may require by rule that parties appeal initial decisions of hearing examiners or bureau decisions to a superior agency authority as a prerequisite to judicial review, but only if the agency provides that the initial decision is inoperative pending such administrative appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows agencies to require internal appeals without forcing issuance of licenses or benefits; the inoperative/pending-appeal requirement prevents automatic deprivation while administrative appeal is pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority to postpone effective date pending judicial review (section 10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending judicial review any agency is authorized, where it finds that justice so requires, to postpone the effective date of any action taken by it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates existing law allowing agencies to stay their actions pending review where justice requires; separate from courts' stay power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court stay power limited to preventing irreparable injury (section 10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every reviewing court is authorized to issue all necessary and appropriate process to postpone the effective date of any agency action or to preserve status or rights pending conclusion of the review proceedings, 'to the extent necessary to prevent irreparable injury.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irreparable injury is the indispensable condition for a stay; mere convenience or maintenance of status quo is insufficient. Courts balance equities and may impose conditions, including security to protect third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on relief available in stays
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10(d) does not permit a court to order the grant of an initial license pending judicial review of an agency's denial, nor to order interim payment of grants or benefits the denial of which is under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stay power is equitable and ancillary to review; it cannot be used to force substantive agency action beyond preserving rights/status pending review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay power vested in 'reviewing court' only after jurisdiction attaches
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'reviewing court' empowered by section 10(d) is the court which has obtained jurisdiction to review the final agency action in accordance with subsections (b) and (c) and applicable statutes; section 10(d) confers no power before submission of final agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents using section 10(d) as a general grant to federal courts to review preliminary or intermediate agency action prior to final agency action review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural provisions for stays (application of general injunction rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10(d) prescribes no procedure for exercising the stay power; general procedural provisions governing preliminary injunctions and restraining orders (e.g., section 381 of Title 28) and the Urgent Deficiencies Act (28 U.S.C. 47) remain applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should apply existing interlocutory injunction procedures when considering stays under section 10(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of judicial review (section 10(e) general statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing court shall decide all relevant questions of law, interpret constitutional and statutory provisions, and determine the meaning or applicability of the terms of any agency action; it shall (A) compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed; and (B) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to meet specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates prior law and codifies the principal functions of courts in reviewing final agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed (section 10(e)(A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed (codifying existing practice under statutes like section 262 of the Judicial Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be effected by writs in the nature of mandamus to require an agency to act or assume jurisdiction, but does not permit courts to substitute their discretion for agency discretion or to exercise administrative duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review ground: arbitrary, capricious, abuse of discretion, or not in accordance with law (section 10(e)(B)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold unlawful and set aside agency action found to be '(1) arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, or otherwise not in accordance with law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates established judicial standards for reviewing reasoned agency decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review ground: contrary to constitutional right, power, privilege, or immunity (section 10(e)(B)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Set aside agency action that is '(2) contrary to constitutional right, power, privilege, or immunity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows courts to invalidate agency actions that infringe constitutional protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review ground: excess of statutory jurisdiction or short of statutory right (section 10(e)(B)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Set aside agency action that is '(3) in excess of statutory jurisdiction, authority, or limitations, or short of statutory right.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets agency actions beyond the scope of statutory grant or failing to afford statutory rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review ground: without observance of procedure required by law (section 10(e)(B)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Set aside agency action that is '(4) without observance of procedure required by law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers failures to follow statutory procedural requirements (notice-and-comment, required hearings, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review ground: unsupported by substantial evidence (section 10(e)(B)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be 'unsupported by substantial evidence in any case subject to the requirements of sections 7 and 8 or otherwise reviewed on the record of an agency hearing provided by statute.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies the substantial-evidence rule; applicable to cases governed by formal hearing-record review and to other statutory hearing-record situations (cites Consolidated Edison v. NLRB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review ground: unwarranted by the facts where facts are subject to trial de novo (section 10(e)(B)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Set aside agency action that is 'unwarranted by the facts to the extent that the facts are subject to trial de novo by the reviewing court.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clause (6) applies only where existing law provides for trial de novo; it does not create a new general right to de novo factfinding where prior practice/relevant statutes require record-review (examples: reparation orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-record review and prejudicial error (harmless error rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: In making determinations the court shall review the whole record or such portions thereof as cited by any party, and due account shall be taken of the rule of prejudicial error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing courts must consider all evidence (not merely that favoring one side) when assessing substantial evidence and should disregard errors that have no substantial bearing on parties' ultimate rights (harmless error).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of agency organization, procedures, and rules (section 3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall separately state and currently publish in the Federal Register descriptions of its central and field organization, statements of the general course and method by which its functions are channeled and determined (including formal and informal procedures), and substantive rules and statements of general policy or interpretations adopted for guidance of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person may be required to resort to organization or procedure not so published; publication covers methods, places to secure information, and forms/instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication or availability of final opinions and orders (section 3(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall publish or, according to published rule, make available to public inspection all final opinions or orders in adjudication of cases (except those confidential for good cause) and all rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and availability of precedential agency adjudications to the public unless confidentiality is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public records access (section 3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters of official record shall, in accordance with published rule, be made available to persons properly and directly concerned, except information held confidential for good cause found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to statutory confidentiality; agencies must have published rules governing access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Rule' and 'Rule making' (section 2(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Rule' means any agency statement of general or particular applicability and future effect designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or to describe organization, procedure, or practice requirements of any agency, including approvals or prescriptions for rates, prices, valuations, etc. 'Rule making' means agency process for the formulation, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition includes many types of agency normative acts; distinguishes rulemaking from adjudication/licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Order' and 'Adjudication' (section 2(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Order' means whole or any part of the final disposition of any agency in any matter other than rule making but including licensing; 'Adjudication' means agency process for the formulation of an order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies coverage of agency final dispositions separate from rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'License' and 'Licensing' (section 2(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'License' includes any agency permit, certificate, approval, registration, charter, membership, statutory exemption or other form of permission; 'Licensing' includes agency processes respecting grant, renewal, denial, revocation, suspension, annulment, withdrawal, limitation, amendment, modification, or conditioning of a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing licensing as agency process brings licensing decisions within APA procedural frameworks when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Sanction' and 'Relief' (section 2(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Sanction' includes prohibitions, requirements, penalties, seizures, assessments, revocation of licenses, or other compulsory/restrictive action; 'Relief' includes grants of money, assistance, recognition of claims/rights, or other beneficial actions on application or petition of any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions identify the substantive actions and remedies that constitute agency action under the APA's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Agency proceeding' (section 2(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Agency proceeding' means any agency process as defined in subsections (c), (d), and (e) (i.e., rulemaking, adjudication, and licensing processes); 'Agency action' includes every agency rule, order, license, sanction, relief, equivalent or denial, or failure to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brings together the processes and actions covered by the Act for application of APA requirements (notice, publication, reviewability, etc.).
